finding.claim: Callback URL stored by subscribe() is later POSTed to by notifyAll() with no validation, so an attacker who can reach /subscribe can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts every minute (blind SSRF; response discarded).
finding.source: src/Jobs.java:13 subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl); callbackUrl is the POST /subscribe body field per the comment at line 12
finding.sink: src/Jobs.java:21-24 URI.create(cb) and client.send(req, ...) in notifyAll()

trace.note: Comment documents the POST /subscribe body containing callbackUrl; the route is not in this repo
subscribe() accepts callbackUrl as a raw String
callbackUrl is stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll() iterates subscriptions.values() and gets the attacker URL back
URI.create(cb) only rejects malformed syntax; no scheme or host check
Outbound POST with a server-controlled payload body
client.send issues the request from the server; the response body is discarded, so the attack is blind

finding.guards_checked: (1) No scheme, host, IP, port, or allowlist check in subscribe() (lines 13-15) or notifyAll() (lines 18-26). (2) No auth check visible in this repo; the /subscribe route and the scheduler are not here, so untrusted reachability is assumed from the comments. (3) HttpClient.newHttpClient() (line 10) defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so redirects cannot pivot to another target. (4) The JDK HttpClient accepts only http and https schemes, so file: and other schemes are blocked, but internal http hosts such as 169.254.169.254 or localhost remain reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none. Nothing in src/Jobs.java validates callbackUrl: subscribe() (lines 13-15) stores it raw, and notifyAll() (lines 19-24) passes it to URI.create and client.send with no scheme, host, or allowlist check. The only validation in the file is the regex in thumb() (line 30), which is on a different path and does not touch subscriptions.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (Jobs.java:12 comment, 13-14 store, 19 iterate, 21 URI.create, 22 POST body, 24 client.send), and no closing guard exists in this repo, but the route that feeds callbackUrl from the request body (POST /subscribe) is not in the repo, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker can reach it (Jobs.java:12 is only a comment) cannot be decided from the code available.
